info.name: D1 API
info.description:
Functional suite for the D1 API across two stacks that run side by side against the same tables:

- **{{claimsApi}}** (/api/d1claims) -- `D1.REST.Router`, from the standalone `claims-api/` tree. No production: a web application and a dispatch class are the whole runtime. Reimplements the eleven endpoints that never needed one, all of which answer straight from IRIS's own tables.
- **{{prodApi}}** (/api/d1) -- `D1.Mock.API.D1API`, the ORIGINAL demo, unchanged. Still serves all nineteen endpoints through `D1.Production`, and is the only route to the seven that stay there -- the five with a business process, plus /admission and /billing, which need the production's configured HIS adapter.

Folders 01-03 exercise the eleven against D1.REST. Folder 04 spot-checks the seven the original keeps to itself.

**Run the folders in order.** Every assertion is pinned to the values `D1.Mock.Data.ClaimLoader` seeds, request 1 reseeds them, and the Writes folder mutates the worklists that the Reads folder asserts on. Because both stacks share the tables, running this suite also moves state the original production would see.

Folder 04 additionally needs D1.Production running and the mock HIS reachable. Folders 00-03 pass against a bare namespace once the web application exists -- `Do ##class(D1.REST.Router).Install()` -- because nothing they touch leaves the instance.

pm.test('room and board carries its coverage item', () => pm.expect(room.coverage_items[0].coverage_code).to.eql('ROOM'));

item.name: 04 Production API (original stack)
item.description: Spot-checks the untouched original at /api/d1, covering the seven endpoints that stay in the production: the five with a business process behind them, plus /admission and /billing, which are only service -> operation but read the HIS through an operation with a configured HTTP outbound adapter. The original also still serves the other eleven; those are exercised against D1.REST in folders 01-03 rather than twice.
